paper.title: Data by Proxy — Material Traces as Autographic Visualizations
paper.venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics, 26(1), 98–108

relevant_section_or_figure: Section 1, “Autographic Visualization,” especially Table 2, “Overview of autographic design operations,” and Section 6.3, “Sensory Accountability—Exploring Data Materiality.”
transferable_principle: Make the conditions and history of knowing perceptible in the state representation itself: construct a state as an indexical material trace of the events that produced it, and preserve enough framing, scale, and annotation for an observer to connect trace to cause. This transfers the paper’s autographic distinction from a symbolic label that stands for a state to a visible state whose form changes because the underlying evidence-generating process changes.
application_to_world_v21: For each task parcel, derive a bounded evidence trace from the live snapshot/SSE stream, worker trace, receipt, and EON time. Let new observations leave a local deposit or layer, worker inference create a visibly connected continuation, and receipt-backed verification create a persistent, high-contrast terminal layer; make stale or conflicting evidence discontinuous or eroding according to EON age. Keep one consistent parcel scale and a compact legend/hover annotation that names the source event and timestamp. This gives unknown/observed/inferred/verified/stale states different material histories while also improving scale and readability without adding unrelated geometry.
falsifier: The principle is falsified if observers cannot reliably distinguish two parcels with different epistemic histories, or if they cannot identify which live event caused a visible state change, without opening a separate debug view; it is also falsified if identical-looking traces result from materially different snapshot/SSE/receipt histories.
fake_evidence: The paper does not evaluate HERAKLES WORLD v21, Three.js, SSE, worker traces, receipts, or EON time.
The proposed parcel trace mappings are an application design inference, not figures or tested results from the paper.
No claim is made that the paper proves material traces are inherently truthful; it explicitly discusses interpretation, rhetorical framing, and the risk of misleading traces.
